name: Pomegranates
tile_uses: Over squash, rice bowls, tacos, the drink
why_now: Southern California grows pomegranates, and they ripen in October and November. A heavy one bought now keeps for weeks and turns anything rich into something brighter.
how_to_choose: Heavy for its size — weight is juice
Slightly angular, flat-sided shapes are the fullest
A dry crack is fine; a soft or wet one is not
buy_this_much: 2. One for the drink, one for scattering. One pomegranate is about a cup of seeds.
price_note: Priced by the piece, so the heavy ones are the deal.

flavor_paths.name: Scattered
flavor_paths.description: Over anything roasted, while it's hot. The default.

flavor_paths.name: Pressed
flavor_paths.description: Juiced through a strainer for the shrub.

weekday_uses: Over roasted delicata, while it's still hot
On a rice bowl with sweet potato and salsa macha
weekend_use: Pressed into the South Park Shrub, with a spoonful of seeds saved for the glass.
storage: Whole, a month in the fridge. Seeded, five days in a covered container.
one_thing_to_learn: Pomegranate is October's lime: something sharp to put against heavier food. Rich things need acid — lemon in the braise, cider vinegar in the shrub, pomegranate on the squash. Same move, different ingredient.
